# TG-LiteNet: where we are after v1, v2 and v2.1

*CSD361 group update, 14 Nov 2026. Every number below is copied from files generated by the code
(`results/` for v2, `results/v21/` for v2.1) or quoted from the papers; nothing was edited by hand.*

---

## 0. The short version

* **The model we recommend showing:** **TG-LiteNet v2.1, ~66K parameters (`H_tglite70k`), with calibre-guided
  test-time scale selection.**
  * 66,125 parameters, 2.73 GFLOPs, about 25 ms per 512×512 image on CPU, 109 KB as INT8.
  * Trained on DRIVE only. Dice on the three unseen datasets (STARE, CHASE_DB1, HRF): **77.9 %**. clDice: **82.0 %**.
  * It is in the same size class as DSAE-Net (78K) and LightVesselNet (75K): 7× smaller than our v2 model and 3× smaller
    than v1.
* **Gap to the state of the art:** about **3–4 Dice points** below DSAE-Net (81.2 %). Almost all of that gap is on HRF
  and CHASE_DB1. On STARE we are level.
* **What is new and holds up:** a label-free rule that picks the processing scale from the predicted vessel width.
  It gives about +1 Dice point on the unseen datasets. The gain is statistically clear and the rule was fixed in
  advance. It helps on HRF, where vessels are relatively thin, and hurts on FIVES. Both are reported.
* **What did not work:** three of the four planned novelties did not show a benefit. We report them as negative
  results. Section 5 gives the details.
* **One rule we must disclose:** our pre-registered size rule picked the 212K `R_lite_w16` model as the formal v2.1
  headline. The 66K model trailed it by 0.0055 Dice on DRIVE-val; the rule allowed 0.005. We show the 66K model as
  the efficiency model and state this openly (Section 6).

---

## 1. How the project evolved

| | v1 (archived, tag `v1-final`) | v2 (rebuild, 11–12 Nov) | v2.1 (follow-up, 13–14 Nov) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Goal | compact, topology-aware vessel model | same, redone with a strict protocol | reach the ~70K size of the SOTA models and add new ideas |
| Training data | DRIVE | DRIVE-train only | DRIVE-train only |
| Model selection | partly after looking at results | DRIVE-val only, protocol frozen before any test | DRIVE-val only, frozen addendum (`protocol/PROTOCOL_v2.1.md`) |
| Test sets | STARE, CHASE, HRF | STARE, CHASE, HRF + FIVES (800 images) | same |
| Seeds | 1–3, unequal | 5 per main stage, 3 per control | 5 (main model), 3 (references, ablations) |
| Main model | 0.21M depthwise "E" | 0.49M U-Net "E" (w8) | **66K U-Net** (channels 8-12-16-24-32) |
| Hardware | Kaggle / Colab | local RTX A4000 | local RTX A4000 |
| Number of runs | ~20 | 76 trainings | 35 trainings + re-evaluation of 7 v2 models |

**Why v2 replaced v1.** v1 had process problems: some analyses were chosen after seeing results; thresholds and
clean-up settings were not fixed in advance; the compact models were undertrained; checkpoints were not kept. v2 fixed
all of these with a written, frozen protocol. v1 numbers are kept below for reference only.

---

## 2. What is in each model

**Common input pipeline (v2 and v2.1).** Every image is rescaled so its field of view is 540 px wide. We keep the green
channel, apply CLAHE and standardise. Training uses 256-px patches, 16 views per step, AdamW 1e-3 with a cosine
schedule and 10,000 iterations. Scores are computed inside the field of view at the dataset's native resolution.

| Model (code name) | Version | What it is | Params |
|---|---|---|---|
| A_unet | v2 | plain U-Net (width 32), Dice + BCE | 31M |
| B_unet_topo | v2 | A + soft-clDice topology loss | 31M |
| C_unet_topo_dg | v2 | B + domain-generalisation (DG) augmentation + consistency loss | 31M |
| D_compact | v2 | C recipe on the compact U-Net (width 8) | 486K |
| **E_tglitenet** | **v2** | D + dropout and MC-dropout uncertainty (**v2 main model**) | 486K |
| ENS_D | v2 | 5-seed ensemble of D | 5×486K |
| **H_tglite70k** | **v2.1** | 66K U-Net + full v2.1 recipe (**recommended model**) | **66K** |
| ENS_H | v2.1 | 5-seed ensemble of H | 5×66K |
| R_lite_w16 | v2.1 | depthwise-separable net (v1-style) with the v2.1 recipe | 212K |
| R_unet_w8 | v2.1 | v2 compact U-Net with the v2.1 recipe | 486K |
| Z_* | v2.1 | the 66K model with one v2.1 ingredient removed (ablations, Section 5) | 66K |

**The v2.1 training recipe** (on top of v2):

1. Topology loss: soft-clDice (λ_topo 0.5) plus a skeleton prediction head.
2. Extra style augmentation: RandConv and low-frequency Fourier-amplitude jitter. These are computed from DRIVE
   images only; no target data is used.
3. **Skeleton consistency** (novelty 4): the augmented view must reproduce the clean view's *centrelines*, not its
   pixels.
4. **Topology-aware distillation** (novelty 3): a teacher made of five 31M v2 "C" models predicts on DRIVE-train.
   The 66K student copies the teacher's pixels (BCE) and its soft centrelines (soft-clDice, λ 1.0).

**Architecture and weight choices** were made on DRIVE-val only:

* The 66K U-Net (`L_cap`) and a 64K two-stage W-Net tied (0.8103 vs 0.8104 val Dice). The U-Net was chosen
  because it is faster on CPU (24.7 vs 29.1 ms).
* The loss weights λ_topo 0.5 and λ_kd_skel 1.0 were chosen from a 2×2 grid using the average of val Dice and clDice.

## 3. The big comparison table: SOTA vs v1 vs v2 vs v2.1

**Column meanings:**

* All scores are in %. **Unseen** = mean over STARE, CHASE_DB1 and HRF, the same three datasets most papers use.
* **Tuned** = threshold and small-fragment removal chosen on DRIVE-val.
* **+ scale sel.** = tuned plus novelty 2.
* **Betti-0 (raw)** = how many more or fewer connected vessel pieces the prediction has than the ground truth,
  averaged per image at threshold 0.5. Lower is better.
* ± = standard deviation over seeds.
* **Published numbers are context, not a ranking.** Training sets, test access, scoring resolution and thresholds
  differ between papers. For example, many papers score downsampled images. Our scores at the network's resolution
  are about 1 point lower than at native resolution (see `results/v21/tables/sota.md`).

## 4. What the comparison tells us

1. **Size.** The 66K model loses only about 1 Dice point against our 486K v2 model (77.9 vs 78.9 with scale
   selection), with 7× fewer parameters and 2.2× fewer FLOPs. It is also the fastest model we have built.
2. **Accuracy against SOTA.**
   * On **STARE** we are level with DSAE-Net (81.0–81.7 vs 81.9).
   * On **CHASE** we are about 4–5 points lower and on **HRF** about 7 points lower. This gap is the same across
     every model we have trained, including the 31M U-Net. So it comes from DRIVE-only training and native-resolution
     scoring on large images, not from model size.
   * We are on par with DGSSA, which trains on several source datasets, and well above WaveRNet.
3. **Connectivity.**
   * The v2.1 models produce fewer broken vessel pieces than v1 and v2: Betti-0 32 (66K) against 43 (v1) and 39 (v2 E).
   * The 66K ensemble reaches 26.5, inside TFFM's published range. Our clDice (about 82) is higher than TFFM's
     (69–74), but TFFM is measured on a different dataset.
4. **Bigger is not much better.** The 31M U-Net beats the 66K model by only about 2 tuned Dice points while costing
   140× the FLOPs. In v2, accuracy stopped improving beyond width 16 (`results/tables/main_tuned.md`).
5. **INT8** keeps accuracy and shrinks the file 2.4×. On this desktop CPU it is slower than FP32, so we claim the
   smaller file, not a speed-up.

## 5. The novelties: what worked and what did not

All criteria were written in `protocol/PROTOCOL_v2.1.md` **before** training. "Clear" means the seed-paired 95 %
interval excludes zero.

| # | Novelty | Idea | Result | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | **Calibre-guided test-time scale selection** | Run the image at 1, 1.5, 2 and 2.5× scale. Keep the scale whose predicted vessel width, measured along the prediction's own centrelines, matches what the model predicts on DRIVE. No labels and no retraining. | Unseen Dice **+1.1 (66K, clear)**, +0.9 (R_lite, clear), +1.0 (R_unet, clear), +0.95 (v2 E, clear). It passed the DRIVE-val safety check for every model. | ✅ **Supported.** It works on HRF (+2.6 to +3.4) and leaves STARE and CHASE almost unchanged. It **hurts FIVES (−2.6 to −6.8)** and the 31M C model (−3.8). |
| 1 | **Connectivity reliability score** | Flag unreliable predictions by counting how fragmented they are (label-free, single pass). Compared with entropy, MC dropout and ensembles. | Primary score `rel_frag` beat MC-dropout uncertainty for v2 E (+0.15 ρ, clear). It did **not** beat ordinary entropy for v2 E (not clear), and was clearly worse than entropy for the 66K model (−0.14). | ❌ **Not met.** Exploratory: two secondary connectivity scores (end-point density, small-fragment share) ranked failures better than entropy for most models (ρ about 0.2–0.3 vs about 0.0–0.2). Worth reporting as a lead, not a result. |
| 3 | **Topology-aware distillation** | The student copies the teacher's soft centrelines, not just its pixels. | Without it: Dice −0.5, clDice +0.2, Betti-0 −11.5. None clear with 3 seeds. | ⚪ **Not shown** |
| 4 | **Skeleton consistency** | The augmented view must reproduce the clean view's centrelines. | Against ordinary pixel consistency: **Dice −0.9 (clearly worse)**, clDice +0.1 (not clear). | ❌ **Harmful to Dice** |
| – | RandConv + Fourier augmentation | Extra style augmentation. | Dice −0.9, not clear. | ⚪ Not shown |
| – | All v2.1 training changes together | Recipe vs the plain v2 recipe on the same 66K net. | Dice −0.8, clDice +0.15, Betti-0 −9 (fewer breaks); none clear. | ⚪ Not shown |

**Plain-language summary.** The gains in v2.1 come from two things: the much smaller architecture, which keeps nearly
all of the accuracy, and novelty 2, the test-time scale rule. The new training losses (novelties 3 and 4) did not add
accuracy. The topology loss and the skeleton head, carried over from v2, are what keep the vessel maps well connected.
With 3 seeds the tests have low power, so "not shown" means *not demonstrated*, not *proven useless*.

Full tables: `results/v21/tables/novelty1_reliability.md`, `novelty2_scale.md` and `ablations.md`.

---

## 6. Which model should we show, and why

**Is v2.1 our best model?**

* It is our **most novel** and **most efficient** model.
* It is **not our most accurate** model. That is still the v2 31M U-Net (78.9 tuned) or the v2 compact ensemble with
  scale selection (79.2).

**Recommendation: present `H_tglite70k` (66K) + calibre-guided scale selection as the TG-LiteNet model.**

* **Same size class as the SOTA lightweight models** (66K vs 75–78K), which was the goal of v2.1. A 486K or 31M
  model cannot be compared with DSAE-Net or LightVesselNet on size.
* **Accuracy is within about 1 point of anything we have built** (77.9 vs 78.9 for v2 E) and close to DGSSA. It is
  about 3–4 points below DSAE-Net, and we say so.
* **It carries the one novelty that holds up**, scale selection, with a clear pre-registered gain. It also has the
  best connectivity per parameter we have measured.
* **Practical:** about 25 ms per image on CPU, 109 KB as INT8, stable across seeds (±0.4, among the lowest spreads
  of any model).

**What we must say alongside it:**

1. The pre-registered size rule picked **R_lite_w16 (212K)** as the formal headline. The 66K model was 0.0055 val
   Dice behind; the rule allowed 0.005. R_lite_w16 is 0.6 points more accurate (78.5) but 3× larger and 4× slower
   on CPU. We show the 66K model as the efficiency point and report R_lite_w16 next to it.
2. Scale selection hurts FIVES; this must be shown next to the gain.
3. Novelties 1, 3 and 4 did not meet their criteria.
4. We train on DRIVE only and test on the other datasets without ever adapting to them. Most of the SOTA numbers come
   from different set-ups.

**Fallback options:**

* If the group would rather lead with the highest accuracy, use **v2 E (486K) + scale selection (78.9)**.
* If they want to lead with the strictest protocol story, use **R_lite_w16 (78.5)**.

The recommended option is the only one that answers the original question: *can a ~70K model trained on one dataset
compete?*
